mappings.note: Identifies Hari Singh as the narrator. Extraction; no character judgement is asked, so not LO-4.
Reads the euphemism 'a fairly successful hand' back to stealing. Information, not the writer's message.
Retrieves the wage (food, not money). Not C-E2.2-LO-4: the value of literacy is not yet in play.
Sadness at the loss of trust rather than of money is the perception that turns him back. LO-4 would be wrong: it is trust, not reading, that is weighed here.
Retrieves the greedy/rich/poor taxonomy of reactions. Extraction.
Retrieves the damp-notes evidence that Anil knew. The significance of his silence is a different item; here only the fact is asked.
The stem quotes both thoughts about writing and then asks what makes him return, so it is literally both outcomes: the worth of sentences over rupees, and the turn.
Why Anil forgoes the police, and how he differs from other employers, is the trust-transforms message argued out. Not LO-4: the demand is the message, not the portrait.
Weighs the two characters against real life. Character appreciation; C-E2.1-LO-2 would need a message to be stated.
Asks whether the struggling-writer detail explains Anil's behaviour -- character read from setting. Not LO-1: the detail is given, the inference is the work.
Imagines the circumstances that make a fifteen-year-old a thief -- character and its background. Not C-E2.2-LO-6, which is about trust, not about how he became a thief.
Setting, explicitly: place, language and the names as evidence. The only item in the chapter that is purely about setting.
Names Ruskin Bond. Extraction.
MCQ form of the same euphemism. Extraction.
The boy's age. Extraction.
Anil's age. Extraction.
Asks how the narrator describes Anil -- simple, kind, easy-going. Character, not a plot fact.
Retrieves that Anil was watching a wrestling match. Extraction.
Retrieves the flattery. The cunning behind it is asked elsewhere; here only the method.
Retrieves the request for employment. Extraction.
Frequency of the name changes. Extraction.
Who the name changes kept him ahead of. Extraction.
The name he gave Anil. Extraction.
A dictionary meaning for 'grunting' with no textual context supplied. No LO covers word-level diction -- LO-1 is about information in the reader, LO-2 about the message -- so the competency is cited.
Retrieves that the first meal was terrible. Extraction.
Infers the verdict on the meal from Anil feeding it to a stray dog -- reading a detail for what it tells. Still extraction, not LO-2.
Retrieves what Anil promised to teach. Not C-E2.2-LO-4, which is reserved for items asking why that teaching outweighs the money.
Word meaning for 'queer'. Same reason as 'grunting': no LO reaches vocabulary, so the competency is the honest citation.
Retrieves that Anil was the most trusting man he had met. Extraction; the consequence of that trust is asked elsewhere.
Retrieves that a greedy man is easiest to rob. Extraction from the taxonomy.
Retrieves what spoils the pleasure of the theft. Extraction.
The sum stolen. Extraction.
That Anil would be sad, not angry, is the thought that starts the turn. Not LO-1: the taxonomy items are the extraction ones, this is the exception that breaks it.
The key is 'he wanted to learn to write' -- precisely valuing the teaching above the six hundred rupees. Not LO-5, which is the process of turning rather than the reason.

Word meaning for 'unlined'. Competency for the vocabulary reason above. NOTE the printed key is wrong: it selects 'not in a line', but in the text 'unlined' describes Anil's untroubled face, which is option C.
MCQ identification of the narrator. Extraction.
Retrieves the promise to teach reading and writing. Recall, so LO-1 rather than C-E2.2-LO-4.
Picks the trait that fits Anil against three that do not. Character.
The boy's real trade. Extraction.
Anil's living, writing for magazines. Extraction.
The thief's assumed name. Extraction.
Who he met at the start. Extraction.

Mapped as extraction about Anil. DEFECT: the printed key says Anil 'was a Wrestler', which contradicts the item in this same chapter keyed 'wrote articles for magazines'. Anil was watching a wrestling match, not wrestling.
The sweet shop below the room. Extraction; a single address is not enough to call it a setting item.
Where the boy was told to sleep. Extraction.
Where Anil kept the money. Extraction.
The moonlight over the bed. Extraction.
The planned departure time. Extraction.
The train he meant to catch. Extraction.
Where he hid the notes. Extraction.
The month of the theft. Extraction.
The clock tower is the place the change of heart happens, and LO-5 asks for the moment it turns to be identified. LO-1 would file the story's hinge as scenery.
The fifty rupees handed back. Extraction; the meaning of the damp note is a separate item.
Reads 'hadn't had much luck of late' in context as recent failure to dupe people. Contextual extraction, unlike the bare dictionary items which took the competency.
What he was grateful for. Extraction.
What Anil did on being paid. Extraction.
What Hari asked for -- work. Extraction.
The reason Anil spares him is that punishment would undo the reform -- the trust message. Not LO-5: this is Anil's choice, not Hari's turn.
The calculated smiles are the boy's cunning -- character. Not LO-1: the item asks for the intention behind a described gesture.
Infers the padded bazaar bills from what the text implies. Extraction by inference.
Why friends were 'more trouble than help' is his character as a man on the run. Not LO-1: the text never states the reason.
Anil overlooking a known breach of trust is the message in action. Not LO-5, which belongs to Hari's side of the same night.
'Addressed the situation by not addressing it at all' -- silence as trust restored. Not LO-4: nothing about reading is at stake.
Retrieves why the writer's income looked odd to him. Extraction.
Why robbing Anil was hard rests on Anil's trusting character set against the greedy and careless types. Not C-E2.2-LO-6: no transformation is claimed yet.
The still-damp fifty-rupee note is the retrievable evidence. The forgiveness it implies is the next item's business.
The food-for-work bargain. Extraction.
The pricking conscience over broken trust is the change of heart itself. Not LO-4: the regret is about trust, not about the lessons.
Answered by the return and the notes replaced under the mattress -- the turn completed. LO-1 would stop at 'he took it to the station'.
Directly asks why he came back. The core LO-5 item.
The signs of forgiveness -- regular pay, the promised lessons -- are trust re-extended. Not LO-5, which ends when he returns.
The three reactions, retrieved in full. Extraction.
Whether he liked the work, with reasons -- his character at Anil's. Not C-E2.2-LO-4: gratitude for the education is only one of the reasons offered.
His self-justifications (out of practice, Anil would waste it, Anil never paid him) are characterisation. Not LO-1: the item asks how he argued, not what happened.
The unexplained hesitation at the moving train IS the moment the change turns, which LO-5 names explicitly.
Asks for evidence that the forgiveness was real -- trust as the transforming force. Not LO-5.
Regular pay so he is not tempted again is trust made practical. Not LO-1: the reason is inferred, not stated.
A diary entry on the human values that transform a person: the trust message, written at length, which is what LO-3 measures.
The five-mark version of the 'neither his lips nor his eyes' question -- message plus extended written form.
Anil's occupation as the source of his insight is character work. Not C-E2.2-LO-6: the question is about Anil's understanding, not about what trust achieved.
'Trace the character arc' in 120 words is character appreciation and the change of heart together, in the long-answer form.
The quoted hesitation at the carriage is handed to the student to explain from inside -- LO-5's moment, as writing.
Anil's values as the cause of the transformation, in 100-120 words. The textbook LO-6 task.
Both halves are retrieval -- the taxonomy of reactions and his guess about Anil -- extended to five marks. Not LO-5: the item stops before he acts on the guess.
Ends on 'the values that stop a person from doing something wrong', which is the trust message generalised. Not LO-4, although Anil's kindness is the evidence.
An explicit character sketch of Hari Singh at five marks.
Names Anil's selfless friendship as the agent of redemption and asks for the journey -- the message and the turn in one item.

The printed extract is the clock-tower passage where whole sentences are weighed against a few hundred rupees, and the sub-items follow that thought to the return. LO-4 and LO-5, not LO-1, because the passage is supplied and only the reasoning is asked.
